studies.name: Ahmed et al. — Teacher professional development for disability inclusion in low- and middle-income Asia-Pacific countries: An evidence and gap map
studies.draft_uses: 2022 publication (Campbell Systematic Reviews 18(4):e1287, published 25 November 2022); cited for: 50 studies found, only 16 of 41 countries reporting evidence, focus on teacher attitudes and understanding of disability, only 3 studies on student mental health, qualitative Vietnamese teacher-training finding, and call to evaluate and publish disability-inclusive TPD evidence
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum was published in 2023 (Campbell Syst Rev, correcting DOI 10.1002/cl2.1287; PubMed PMID for corrigendum: 36913230). The draft itself acknowledges this correction exists but states it could not read it, and formally disclaims reliance on this source — yet the body text cites it [2] for multiple specific figures. The content of the corrigendum could not be retrieved; it is unknown whether the corrected figures include any of those the draft quotes.
studies.what_changed: Cannot confirm. The corrigendum exists (2023) and its scope is unknown. The draft simultaneously disclaims and uses this source, creating an internal inconsistency. The figures at risk are: '50 studies', '16 of 41 countries', '3 studies on mental health', and the Vietnamese qualitative finding — none of these can be verified against the corrected version.

studies.name: Saran et al. — Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries
studies.draft_uses: 2020 publication (Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(1):e1070, published 9 January 2020); cited for: studies focusing on 'fixing individuals' rather than infrastructure/institutions/social barriers, significant gap in study quality especially for impact evaluations, and limited evidence from low-income countries
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum was published 12 July 2020 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(3):e1104, correcting DOI 10.1002/cl2.1070). The corrigendum corrected income-group distribution figures: 'Over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries' was changed to 'Almost half (n=50)… closely followed by upper-middle income countries (n=48)', and corrected the Thailand study count to n=6. No further update or new version of the EGM was found. The draft acknowledges the correction exists and disclaims reliance on this source, but cites it [3] in the body for qualitative gap claims (not the corrected income-group counts).
studies.what_changed: The 2020 corrigendum corrected income-group impact-evaluation counts (upper-middle income n=48 not n=50; 'almost half' not 'over half' from lower-middle income; Thailand n=6). The draft does not quote these corrected figures — it cites Saran [3] only for qualitative gap characterisations (focus on individuals, quality gaps, limited low-income-country evidence), which were not affected by the corrigendum. No post-2020 update to the EGM itself was found.
